title: LG defends smart-TV features amid audio surveillance allegations
author: Hoda Sherif
content:
![BERLIN, GERMANY - SEPTEMBER 02: A visitor wears 3D glasses while watching a presentation of 3D Smart TV at the LG stand at the IFA 2011 consumer technology trade fair on the first day of the fair's official opening on September 2, 2011 in Berlin, Germany. The IFA 2011 will be open to the public from September 2-7. (Photo by Sean Gallup/Getty Images)](https://www.aljazeera.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/getty_6aa1aae49b-1788979940.jpg?resize=770%2C513&quality=80)
South Korean consumer-electronics company LG has denied allegations that its smart televisions record ambient conversations, listen while on standby and store recordings for later transmission.
On Wednesday, the company told Al Jazeera that voice data is only recorded when a user presses and holds the voice button on the TV remote or activates its “Hi LG” wake word, after the user has activated the Far-Field voice recognition feature.
“Other than these instances, the TVs do not collect or record ambient conversations,” LG said, adding that voice data is only processed via explicit user commands.
“The audio is immediately deleted if the wake word is not recognised,” the company said.
The statement comes after a 135-minute investigative report released on Monday by a popular tech media outlet and YouTube channel, Gamers Nexus, with Level1Techs and independent security researchers. The investigation examined LG televisions’ data collection and security systems, raising questions about how the devices handle users’ private information.
By analysing network traffic and software, the researchers purport to have discovered that these televisions actively track users and harvest a glut of local network data, including audio transcripts.
Inside LG’s controversial tracking system
Gamers Nexus said its researchers were able to record audio through an LG television while it was in a state of hibernation, meaning that even if the microphone switch on the TV is turned off, other microphones exposed to the TV might not be, such as the remote.
The result, Gamers Nexus says, is “216,000,000 Spy TVs” in the US alone.
On its website, LG says it has 49 million smarts TVs in the US and 216 million globally.
Recorded background noise in the room, including as far as 12 metres (40 feet) away from the TV, was also being archived, they said.
Yash Vekaria, a computer science researcher at the University of California, Davis, says that because TVs stay in homes for years, often past their update support, “prompt patching from LG matters”.
“This vulnerability can allow sniffing [of] much more critical conversations … Imagine government officials discussing national security in their hotel room [next to an] LG TV”, Vekaria said.
The researchers further alleged that unmatched wake-word interactions or unclear sounds could remain stored locally, transcribed and preserved on the device as plain text in case the local network is disconnected and uploaded later to LG servers.
Copies can stay in temporary storage spaces, known as buffers, without the user knowing, Vekaria said.
Privacy risks generally stem from poor design and selective disclosure. The more disconcerting threat lies in a compromised device, Vekaria added, which could be made to execute any command its hardware allows.
The researchers also said they found text transcripts derived from audio captured by the television, even after 10-15 seconds of silence after invoking “Hi LG”.
The claims have not been independently verified by Al Jazeera.
“It raises a question of purpose,” says Vekaria, “a voice command is only useful in real time, so audio queued for later upload is presumably being kept for something else, such as logging, analytics or model training. LG should explain what”.
Vekaria says he is not aware of any concrete evidence that ambient audio or transcripts feed into LG’s advertising or profiling systems.
“What we do know is that LG runs an advertising business built on household data, including the Automatic Content Recognition [ACR] tracking documented in our research, and that its voice pipeline appears to capture and retain more than users would expect.”
Still, there may be simpler explanations, he says, “such as diagnostics or improving speech recognition … but even those involve keeping recordings from people’s homes without meaningful consent”.
The smart home is listening
The researchers also said that the televisions scanned home networks for other devices and collected information including internal IP addresses, nearby Wi-Fi networks and location data.
LG said scanning for nearby devices is a “standard” smart-TV function.
Device discovery can serve “legitimate functions” such as screen casting, media sharing and connecting smart-home products, like Amazon’s Alexa, said Anna Maria Mandalari, a lecturer in communications and networking at University College London.
LG stated that ACR, voice recognition and interest-based advertising are all “separate features”, each requiring “explicit user opt-in consent” and each of which can be disabled through the TV’s settings.
Depending on how device discovery is implemented, Mandalari said, a television may “obtain the names, addresses, manufacturers and types of other devices on a household network” – information that can reveal the composition of a home and help “create a broader profile of its occupants”.
LG’s advertising arm, LG Ad Solutions, has openly marketed the breadth of information it can derive from connected households. Corporate videos featured in the Gamers Nexus investigation show LG representatives saying: “We know who is in the LG household,” and, “We know which devices are there.”
LG told Al Jazeera that it was “committed to providing transparency” and that it rejected “deceptive practices”.
summary: LG has denied allegations from an investigative report by Gamers Nexus and other researchers claiming that its smart televisions record and store ambient conversations while on standby. The company stated that voice data is only collected when explicitly commanded through the remote or wake word, and that unrecognized audio is deleted immediately. However, researchers argued that the voice pipeline and local buffering retain more data than expected, and raised security concerns regarding network scanning and privacy.
key_points: LG denied allegations that its smart TVs record ambient conversations and standby audio, stating that voice data is only processed via explicit user commands.
An investigation by Gamers Nexus and researchers claimed that LG smart TVs track users, harvest local network data, and potentially archive background noise.
Researchers alleged that unmatched wake-word interactions and transcripts can be stored locally in temporary buffers for later upload.
LG stated that its TVs scan home networks as a standard function and that features like Automatic Content Recognition, voice recognition, and interest-based ads require explicit opt-in consent.

title: Apple’s new iPhone camera mode promises to prove your photo isn’t AI
author: Emma Roth
content:
Apple is launching a new way to prove that the picture you took isn’t manipulated by AI. A new feature, called “Reference Image,” will arrive with the iPhone 18 Pro lineup later this month and is supposed to use the device’s new camera sensor to “sign every pixel it sees.”
Apple’s new iPhone camera mode promises to prove your photo isn’t AI
A new sensor in the iPhone 18 Pro will authenticate photos captured in Reference mode.
![268734_iPhone_2026_event_handson_ADiBenedetto_0023](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/268734_iPhone_2026_event_handson_ADiBenedetto_0023.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0%2C0%2C100%2C100&w=2400)
![268734_iPhone_2026_event_handson_ADiBenedetto_0023](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/268734_iPhone_2026_event_handson_ADiBenedetto_0023.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0%2C0%2C100%2C100&w=2400)
The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will only authenticate photos when placed into Reference mode. Once the camera captures signed sensor data, Apple says its Private Cloud Compute will develop it “into an unalterable reference image” that can be viewed in the Photos app. You’ll be able to compare the reference image with other versions of the photo to see if any edits were made.
![You can compare the Reference Image to other versions of the photo.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/reference-image.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0%2C0%2C100%2C100&w=2400)
As AI-generated images and videos become more realistic, several new standards have emerged to label images not created by a human, such as SynthID, C2PA, and Meta’s Content Seal. Apple is putting a twist on these methods by building authentication directly into its hardware.
Apple is letting developers access a Reference Image API across iOS, iPadOS, and macOS, which could eventually allow users to inspect these digitally signed photos in third-party apps. The company says the iPhone 18 Pro lineup won’t come with its Reference Image feature at launch in the European Union, but it says users in the region will still be able to “develop and view” them in iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and macOS 27.
summary: Apple is introducing a new camera feature called "Reference Image" for the iPhone 18 Pro lineup to prove photos are genuine and unmanipulated by AI. The tool utilizes a new camera sensor to sign captured pixel data, which Apple's Private Cloud Compute then develops into an unalterable reference image for comparison. Developers will also gain access to a Reference Image API to support inspection of these digitally signed photos in third-party applications across Apple's operating systems.
key_points: Apple is launching the Reference Image feature with the iPhone 18 Pro lineup to authenticate authentic photos.
The new feature uses a device sensor to sign pixel data and processes it via Private Cloud Compute into an unalterable image.
Users can compare the reference image with other versions of a photo to detect edits or AI manipulation.
A Reference Image API will be available to developers for iOS, iPadOS, and macOS.
The feature will not be available at launch in the European Union, though users there can still develop and view reference images in future OS versions.

title: The V8 is back – meet Mercedes' mad new 637bhp CLE | Autocar
author: Charlie Martin
content:
Mercedes-AMG has transplanted a V8 into the CLE to create one of its most extreme cars yet in a return to its hot-rodding roots.
Called the CLE 646 Spezialanfertigung - special order - it has been conceived as the most driver-focused version of Mercedes' premium coupe.
The model starts out as a CLE 53 before being extensively modified to become the 646, mirroring the production of historic AMG models before the brand became integrated into Mercedes-Benz.
![](https://www.autocar.co.uk/sites/autocar.co.uk/files/styles/body-image/public/merecedes-cle-amg-646-328.jpg?itok=UPqnfM-T)
Described by AMG as an engineering-led project, it was originally a test mule produced behind closed doors.
It swaps the 3.0-litre straight six found in the only current AMG derivative of the CLE, the 53, for Mercedes new M177 Evo V8 powerplant.
The 4.0-litre twin-turbo V8, which made its debut in the facelifted S-Class, is boosted to 637bhp - equivalent to 646PS, hence the name - and 627lb ft. It is fitted with a bespoke Akrapovic titanium exhaust, which is said to maximise the "emotional focus" of the powerplant.
![](https://www.autocar.co.uk/sites/autocar.co.uk/files/styles/body-image/public/merecedes-cle-amg-646-330.jpg?itok=JIWIfDvs)
The V8-powered CLE also ditches four-wheel drive for rear-drive to maximise its performance on track, while shedding weight.
The 646 brings several other lightweighting measures traditionally reserved for track-focused machines, including carbonfibre bodywork, polycarbonate windows and even a different 12V battery. Meanwhile, the body has been reinforced to improve its rigidity, and a roll-cage has been integrated into its structure.
The revisions mean the 646 weighs 1895kg - 30kg lighter than the CLE 53, despite packing a larger and significantly heavier engine. According to AMG, 170kg was stripped from the car in total.
summary: Mercedes-AMG has introduced the CLE 646 Spezialanfertigung, an extreme, driver-focused coupe featuring a twin-turbo V8 engine. Starting as a modified CLE 53 test mule, the car replaces the standard straight-six engine and four-wheel-drive system with a 637bhp V8 and rear-wheel drive. Despite the heavier engine, comprehensive lightweighting measures—including carbonfibre bodywork, polycarbonate windows, and a smaller battery—help the car weigh 30kg less than the CLE 53.
key_points: The CLE 646 Spezialanfertigung is powered by a 4.0-litre twin-turbo M177 Evo V8 producing 637bhp and 627lb ft of torque.
The car ditches four-wheel drive in favor of a rear-wheel-drive setup optimized for track performance.
It features lightweight measures such as carbonfibre bodywork, polycarbonate windows, and a bespoke Akrapovic titanium exhaust.
The body has been reinforced with an integrated roll-cage to improve rigidity.
Despite the larger engine, the 646 weighs 1895kg, making it 30kg lighter than the CLE 53.

title: Hands-On With Apple's First Foldable Phone: The iPhone Duo Redefines the Formula
author: Eric Zeman
content:
![](https://sm.pcmag.com/t/pcmag_uk/news/h/hands-on-w/hands-on-with-apples-first-foldable-phone-the-iphone-duo-red_anmm.1920.jpg) (Credit: Eric Zeman)
CUPERTINO—With the iPhone Duo, Apple finally enters the foldable market. I tried it at the company's Surprise and Shine event; the passport-shaped iPhone Duo goes crease-to-crease against the similarly sized Galaxy Z Fold 8 from Samsung, which has been available for about a month, as well as strong entries from Google and Motorola. The iPhone Duo promises everything you've come to expect from an iPhone and more, but can Apple's first take on a foldable match those from industry veterans?
Design: Not Terribly Different From Others
Nothing about the iPhone Duo is a surprise in person. I don't say that because nearly everything about it was leaked ahead of time, but because other companies have been fielding flexible devices for many years now. Samsung, Apple's chief rival, brought the original Galaxy Z Fold to market in mid-2019 and is now on its eighth-generation hardware. The space is all but mature, and Apple is way late. ![](https://sm.pcmag.com/pcmag_uk/photo/a/apple-ipho/apple-iphone-duo_r7yb.jpg) (Credit: Eric Zeman)
The phone is about the same size and shape as a passport, a decision Apple arrived at with strict attention to screen aspect ratios. Though the Z Fold 8 shares this shape, many others do not. The Z Fold 8 Ultra is a taller, narrower book-style folding device, as is the Google Pixel 11 Pro Fold and Motorola Razr Fold. A number of similar-style phones are available from Chinese makers overseas. ![](https://sm.pcmag.com/pcmag_uk/photo/a/apple-ipho/apple-iphone-duo_dyt1.jpg) (Credit: Eric Zeman)
It's got a metal frame, glass front and rear surfaces, a hinge that folds 180 degrees, and a large screen hiding within. The buttons and ports are scattered around the side edges. It's nice and thin when open, but rather thick when closed. These are the defining characteristics of the device class. It's heavier than Samsung's foldables, but lighter than Google and Motorola's. ![](https://sm.pcmag.com/pcmag_uk/photo/a/apple-ipho/apple-iphone-duo_za7c.jpg) (Credit: Eric Zeman)
Anyone who is not used to folding phones will have to climb a bit of a learning curve if they switch from their normal iPhone to the Duo. It's a paradigm shift, for sure.
Experience: The Best First-Gen Foldable I've Used
As unsurprising as the basic design is, the overall experience is a step up from what I've seen from competitors. It's almost like Apple took two iPhone Airs (my personal favorite Apple design) and slapped them together. The hardware's slick execution is absolutely top-notch.
![](https://sm.pcmag.com/pcmag_uk/photo/a/apple-ipho/apple-iphone-duo_zu8m.jpg) (Credit: Eric Zeman)
Apple clearly studied the designs of old foldables. The hinge is made from hundreds of parts and protected with a titanium shield. It includes spring mechanisms that help open it and magnets that help hold it shut. The magnets have just enough strength to keep the halves connected when you want them closed, but aren't so strong that you can't pry the halves apart. Once you get them apart slightly, the springs take over, and the machinations within flow through all 180 degrees. Even then, you can stop, and the hinge will maintain any angle you set.
The hinge on the Razr Fold feels creaky in comparison, though Google and Samsung's most recent phones have smooth hinges. Apple hasn't said how many times it can fold open and closed, but it feels incredibly solid. ![](https://sm.pcmag.com/pcmag_uk/photo/a/apple-ipho/apple-iphone-duo_zhtk.jpg) (Credit: Eric Zeman)
Then there's the general level of fit and finish: It's Apple all the way. The phone is made from the same high-quality materials as its Pro iPhones—titanium, stainless steel, aluminum, and Apple's Ceramic Shield—and assembled as tightly and firmly as anything Apple makes. It meets IP68 protection against dust and water, a huge benefit for such an expensive piece of gear. Google and Motorola match the rating, but Samsung's have a less-protection IP48 rating.
All the buttons and keys are high-grade and feel great to use. I'm bummed the phone doesn't have Face ID, but Apple's implementation of Touch ID (fingerprint scanner) is the best in the business.
The raw experience of using the iPhone Duo is simply terrific. I can't wait to use it for more than just a few moments.
Screens: Adaptability Required
The screens are going to take some getting used to. I'm a seasoned user of foldables, and I'm still adjusting to the Z Fold 8's size and shape. The Duo's outer screen is 5.4 inches, and the inner screen is 7.6 inches. Neither measurement is the largest, but they share the same aspect ratio, so flipping between them feels seamless, no matter which app you have on the screen. (Samsung made the same decisions with the Z Fold 8's design.)
![](https://sm.pcmag.com/pcmag_uk/photo/a/apple-ipho/apple-iphone-duo_tgfy.jpg) (Credit: Eric Zeman)
The outer screen is much shorter and a bit wider than the screen on a phone like the iPhone 18 Pro Max. You lose a noticeable amount of vertical space for apps to fill, but you have a wider space for typing. The inner screen is similar to the Flex Titanium display of the Z Fold 8 and Z Fold 8 Ultra. It's made of 10 layers, including a titanium plate for rigidity. One thing I found most surprising in the top layer is its nano-etched texture, which scatters light, giving it an almost matte appearance. There are no reflections, no glare. This saps some of the brilliance from the experience, but I think the trade-off for usability is well worth it.
It's utterly great for watching 16:9 video, and easily handles two side-by-side apps when you need to multitask. I like that the screen supports the Apple Pencil USB-C.
DuoOS: A New Take on iOS
DuoOS doesn't exist (we made that up), but it should. iOS 27 on the iPhone Duo introduces a significant number of changes to the user interface, so much so that it leans toward iPadOS. ![](https://sm.pcmag.com/pcmag_uk/photo/a/apple-ipho/apple-iphone-duo_cq4w.jpg) (Credit: Eric Zeman)
Apple moved many of iOS's traditional controls from the top or bottom of the screen to the right edge, where you can easily tap them with your thumb. (No word from Apple yet on whether or not these UI elements move to the left for left-handed people.)
The camera app gets a lot of changes, though none of them are actually new compared with other folding phones. You can use the outer screen to show your subject what the phone might look like before you take it, swap between the outer and inner cameras with ease, and pose the phone to help take selfies. ![](https://sm.pcmag.com/pcmag_uk/photo/a/apple-ipho/apple-iphone-duo_54zv.jpg) (Credit: Eric Zeman)
Multitasking feels as simple and as uncomplicated as it could possible be. In fact, I'd say Apple's software comes across as more slight in this respect, compared with Android, even though Android vendors have been iterating on this for years. The phone supports up to two side-by-side apps when the phone is open in landscape orientation. If you rotate the phone 90 degrees, the most recent app takes over the entire screen. The second app reappears if you rotate the phone back. You can also float a picture-in-picture window on top of these with apps like YouTube or Netflix.
Apple has released new APIs to help developers adapt their apps to Duo's UI. I can't wait to see more customization.
Are You Ready?
Folding phones are outrageously expensive, and the iPhone Duo is no different. The starting price is $1,999 for the model with 256GB of storage. The 512GB model costs $2,199, the 1TB model costs $2,599, and the 2TB model costs $3,199 (that's more than many high-end MacBook Pro configurations). The phone comes in white and a deep blue.
If you have the pocket change, you're going to have to dig deep for the change in everyday usability. Folding phones just hit differently, and not always for the better. You'll find compromises—often in battery life and camera performance.
Is it worth it? Well, I can't fully answer that until we test the phone. None of Apple's hands on demos included speed tests, radio evaluations, or battery rundowns. For that, and our final verdict, you'll have to wait for our full review. Preorders for the iPhone Duo begin on Oct. 16, and it goes on sale Oct. 23.
In the meantime, check out all our on-the-ground Apple iPhone coverage.
summary: Apple enters the foldable phone market with the passport-shaped iPhone Duo, featuring a 5.4-inch outer screen and a 7.6-inch inner screen with a nano-etched, anti-glare matte top layer. Despite arriving late to a mature market, Apple delivers a top-notch hardware execution complete with an IP68 dust and water resistance rating, a smooth 180-degree hinge, and a specialized iOS user interface. The device starts at $1,999 for the 256GB model and goes on sale on October 23, following preorders on October 16.
key_points: The iPhone Duo features a passport-sized design with a 5.4-inch outer screen and a 7.6-inch inner screen sharing the same aspect ratio.
The device includes a robust 180-degree hinge built from hundreds of parts, protected by a titanium shield, and features spring and magnet mechanisms.
It comes with an IP68 dust and water resistance rating and utilizes Apple's Touch ID fingerprint scanner instead of Face ID.
Pricing begins at $1,999 for the 256GB base model and scales up to $3,199 for the 2TB version.
Preorders begin on October 16, with the official launch scheduled for October 23.

title: People call out ‘creepy’ new Apple feature and say it feels straight out of 'Black Mirror'
author: Olivia Burke
content:
![New Apple Watch feature labelled 'straight out of Black Mirror' as consumers creeped out](https://resizer.ladbiblegroup.com/unsafe/rs:fit:3840:0:0:0/g:sm/q:70/aHR0cHM6Ly9ldS1pbWFnZXMuY29udGVudHN0YWNrLmNvbS92My9hc3NldHMvYmx0Y2Q3NGFjYzFkMGE5OWYzYS9ibHQ0ODY2OWQ0MTU4MmQ5YThhLzZhYTI1NDg3NDUyYmI3N2ZiMTEwYjg4YS9hcHBsZS1pcGhvbmUuanBn.webp)
Apple is introducing a new feature designed to help forgetful folks, but the majority of people think it's invasive rather than innovative.
The tech giant unveiled its latest iPhone, AirPods and Apple Watches on Wednesday (9 September), as well as the advanced AI capabilities of Siri.
Apple boss John Ternus, who stepped into Tim Cook's shoes at the beginning of the month, debuted the company's first-ever foldable iPhone as well as revealing its controversial price tag.
But people are more preoccupied with him introducing 'Audio Intelligence', a new feature that will be rolled out with the Apple Watch Series 12, which promises to provide 'advanced health and fitness features'.
Advert
"Apple Watch Series 12 is the most advanced health and fitness companion we’ve ever created," Apple’s vice president of Worldwide Apple Watch Product Marketing, Kaiann Drance, said.
![The Apple Watch Series 12 will launch later this month (AP/PA Image)](https://resizer.ladbiblegroup.com/unsafe/rs:fit:3840:0:0:0/g:sm/q:70/aHR0cHM6Ly9ldS1pbWFnZXMuY29udGVudHN0YWNrLmNvbS92My9hc3NldHMvYmx0Y2Q3NGFjYzFkMGE5OWYzYS9ibHQ3ZjczOGQwY2U4YmIyZGJjLzZhYTI1MjcwNjFmZDczMzhiMTNmNjEzOS9hcHBsZS13YXRjaC5qcGc.webp)
"With our new Health Sensing System and S11 chip, Apple Watch Series 12 gives you meaningful insights, like readiness, so you can better understand how to take on your day and care for your health, plus intelligence features that make everyday life easier.
"And it’s all wrapped in a beautifully thin, light design you’ll love wearing all day and night."
Those who enjoy sporting this sort of tech on their wrist will also be able to 'stay alert to important sounds', while also 'staying present', according to Apple.
That's because this new Apple Watch, which costs upwards of £369, will boast a feature known as 'Audio Intelligence'.
Apple describes this as a way to 'help users stay aware of the world around them, catch what they missed, and remember key moments - with user control, privacy, security, and accessibility at the centre of its design'.
![The new Apple Watch comes with a wide range of never-before-seen features (Benjamin Fanjoy/Getty Images)](https://resizer.ladbiblegroup.com/unsafe/rs:fit:3840:0:0:0/g:sm/q:70/aHR0cHM6Ly9ldS1pbWFnZXMuY29udGVudHN0YWNrLmNvbS92My9hc3NldHMvYmx0Y2Q3NGFjYzFkMGE5OWYzYS9ibHQ4ZGNhZDllYjM1OTMwMjEzLzZhYTI4OTA0OTlkZDliNGQ4MTZlMjk5Yy9hcHBsZS13YXRjaC5qcGc.webp)
New features of the Apple Watch
The watches have a built-in microphone, which will be put to work a lot more than the ones in previous models.
Apple explained that this new generation of timepieces will be able to alert users who are deaf or hard of hearing of important sounds, such as sirens, alarms, doorbells, or a baby crying, by using on-device intelligence to notify users when they’re detected.
The 'Live Rewind' feature explained
The California-based company also announced a controversial feature called 'Live Rewind', which was created to 'help users recall what was just said in conversation'.
Apple said: "A double press of the Digital Crown shows the previous 15 seconds of a conversation as a text snippet, so the user can catch something they may have missed or are less familiar with. Users can ask Siri about the content of the text or save it to the Siri app to revisit later.
![The 'Audio Intelligence' feature has proved controversial (David Paul Morris/Bloomberg via Getty Images)](https://resizer.ladbiblegroup.com/unsafe/rs:fit:3840:0:0:0/g:sm/q:70/aHR0cHM6Ly9ldS1pbWFnZXMuY29udGVudHN0YWNrLmNvbS92My9hc3NldHMvYmx0Y2Q3NGFjYzFkMGE5OWYzYS9ibHRkMmZhNzNmZDhlMjhhYzk4LzZhYTI1MzM0OThjZjc3MWY0MDdjMzFhZC9hcHBsZS13YXRjaC1hdWRpby1pbnRlbGxpZ2VuY2UuanBn.webp)
"Siri Recap, which can create high-level summaries of conversations that users can review later to jog their memory. When Siri Recap is turned on, after a conversation, Apple Intelligence automatically generates a title and key points in the new Siri app, allowing users to be more present and engaged in the moment."
An 'incredibly creepy' concept
The idea of Apple Watches now recording conversations has not gone down well with a lot of people, as many have suggested it's Black Mirror-esque.
Taking to social media, one person said: "Do they not realise how incredibly creepy this is?"
A second wrote: "Just gonna have to tattoo 'I do not consent to being recorded' on my forehead at this point."
And a third added: "This was literally a Black Mirror episode."
Others were more welcoming to the introduction of 'Audio Intelligence', but the overwhelming majority weren't thrilled by the idea.
Apple said that this new feature does not create or store audio recordings, while insisting that operating systems, apps, the user, or Apple cannot access them.
![Apple's CEO John Ternus unveiled the latest gadgets on Wednesday (David Paul Morris/Bloomberg via Getty Images)](https://resizer.ladbiblegroup.com/unsafe/rs:fit:3840:0:0:0/g:sm/q:70/aHR0cHM6Ly9ldS1pbWFnZXMuY29udGVudHN0YWNrLmNvbS92My9hc3NldHMvYmx0Y2Q3NGFjYzFkMGE5OWYzYS9ibHQ1YTE0MjY0N2JjMDVmNzgzLzZhYTI1M2MzZmZmMWJmMTliOTUwMDcxNi9hcHBsZS5qcGc.webp)
How Audio Intelligence works
Explaining how it works, the firm said: "This is because the S11 chip on Apple Watch Series 12 includes Secure Exclave, a dedicated hardware-isolated compartment that processes audio in complete isolation from the rest of the system, then immediately deletes it. Users are in control and can choose whether to opt in to each Audio Intelligence feature. They can decide exactly where and when Siri Recap takes notes, and can turn Siri Recap on or off at any time, right from Control Center.
"By design, Audio Intelligence features do not identify and attribute speakers, to protect the privacy of both the user and those around them. Siri Recap produces a brief, high-level summary of conversations — not a transcript — and is designed to exclude sensitive information like financial information or government-assigned identifiers. Live Rewind plays an audible chime when it is being used, even if Apple Watch is on silent, and shows a full-display animation and microphone indicator so people nearby can hear and see that the feature has been activated."
So, you might want to listen out for that audible chime before you go spilling your secrets when the Apple Watch Series 12 launches on 18 September.
What else did Apple announce at its autumn event?
Aside from its new watches, the tech company also unveiled a plethora of new tech and upgrades. Here's the full rundown.
iPhone duo
![(Apple)](https://resizer.ladbiblegroup.com/unsafe/rs:fit:3840:0:0:0/g:sm/q:70/aHR0cHM6Ly9ldS1pbWFnZXMuY29udGVudHN0YWNrLmNvbS92My9hc3NldHMvYmx0Y2Q3NGFjYzFkMGE5OWYzYS9ibHQyNTZmNzJhMzBjMGVlMTllLzZhYTI1ZmQyZjY3MWJhN2M1MmIxMWU5Ny9pbWFnZV8oMilfKDEpLndlYnA.webp)
Its big-ticket item of the event was the iPhone Duo, the first new folding iPhone, which it claims will do the job of two gadgets in one.
When unfolded, it looks more like the size of a tablet, but when folded up it's more the size of a large phone.
Apple boasted the Duo had 'up to 40 percent higher stiffness' compared to other devices on the market, and said it meant that the new iPhone wouldn't become damaged over time when it was being folded and unfolded.
On the inside, it's got an A20 Pro chip for performance, and has their most advanced technology stuffed inside a foldable design, and it's going to be eSIM only.
Two batteries are inside the device, which Apple says gives you up to 24 hours per charge when using both of the screens, and they claim you can charge it up halfway in just a matter of minutes.
While the camera has been adapted so the phone can be folded over, it's still of the same calibre as the one that comes with the iPhone 18 range.
iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max
![(Apple)](https://resizer.ladbiblegroup.com/unsafe/rs:fit:3840:0:0:0/g:sm/q:70/aHR0cHM6Ly9ldS1pbWFnZXMuY29udGVudHN0YWNrLmNvbS92My9hc3NldHMvYmx0OTQ5ZWE4ZTE2ZTQ2MzA0OS9ibHQ4NjU0N2NjOTA1NTkyMDM5LzZhYTI1MzIzMjQ3ZWRjYmI3YzY3YmU5Zi9BcHBsZS1pUGhvbmUtMTgtUHJvLWNvbG9yLWxpbmV1cC0yNjA5MDlfYmlnLmpwZy5sYXJnZV8yeC5qcGc.webp)
Among the new features, Apple says its new 18 Pro Max has the longest battery life of any iPhone to date, while the iPhone 18 Pro is said to have the same battery life as the 17 Pro Max, so it should still be fairly decent. The tech giant claims it'll take just 15 minutes to charge the phone to 50 percent using a wired connection.
As well as this, the new A20 is said to deliver 'up to 40 percent improved graphics performance', while the company has also introduced a new feature called Apple Reference Image, which helps to verify the authenticity of photos.
“With iPhone 18 Pro, we’ve made advancements to the areas our users care about most: camera, performance, battery, and intelligence. And we didn’t just make incremental improvements in these areas — we took huge leaps forward to create the best Pro iPhone we’ve ever made,” said Greg Joswiak, Apple’s senior vice president of Worldwide Marketing.
New and improved Health app
![(Apple)](https://resizer.ladbiblegroup.com/unsafe/rs:fit:3840:0:0:0/g:sm/q:70/aHR0cHM6Ly9ldS1pbWFnZXMuY29udGVudHN0YWNrLmNvbS92My9hc3NldHMvYmx0OTQ5ZWE4ZTE2ZTQ2MzA0OS9ibHQ5NzkyZGJkNjliMDRlN2JjLzZhYTI1NTYxOGE5NWZhNmY2NGEyMWNmMi9BcHBsZS1pUGhvbmUtMTgtUHJvLUFwcGxlLVdhdGNoLVNlcmllcy0xMi1yZWRlc2lnbmVkLUhlYWx0aC1hcHAtMjYwOTA5X2lubGluZS5qcGcubGFyZ2VfMnguanBn.webp)
The announcement had a big focus on health and fitness, so it's no surprise the company has tried to elevate its Health app using Apple Intelligence.
New features include the all-new readiness score, a Health Age score, a new Longevity tab and personalised fitness suggestions based on your scores.
According to Apple, its new Health app also allows users to take in-depth assessments of how well their bodies are moving.
AirPods 5
![(Apple)](https://resizer.ladbiblegroup.com/unsafe/rs:fit:3840:0:0:0/g:sm/q:70/aHR0cHM6Ly9ldS1pbWFnZXMuY29udGVudHN0YWNrLmNvbS92My9hc3NldHMvYmx0OTQ5ZWE4ZTE2ZTQ2MzA0OS9ibHRlNWU2MTkyNTA1Zjc2MGY0LzZhYTI1MzBjMGIwNmIwMmNhMzFhNzM5ZS9BcHBsZS1BaXJQb2RzLTUtaGVyby0yNjA5MDlfYmlnLmpwZy5sYXJnZV8yeC5qcGc.webp)
Apple says its new AirPods deliver 'the industry’s best Active Noise Cancellation (ANC) in an open-ear design and even better sound quality' which 'removes up to 50 percent more external noise compared to AirPods 4'.
There are two options customers can go for: the slightly cheaper entry-level AirPods 5, or the AirPods 5 with Wireless Charging Case, which the company says 'adds longer battery life and on-stem volume control'.
Topics: Apple, Technology, Weird, iPhone
summary: Apple unveiled its new Apple Watch Series 12 along with the iPhone Duo, iPhone 18 Pro models, AirPods 5, and updated health features. A central addition to the new watch is 'Audio Intelligence,' featuring tools like Live Rewind and Siri Recap that process and summarize conversations. While Apple highlighted privacy controls and hardware-isolated processing, many consumers took to social media to call the feature invasive and reminiscent of 'Black Mirror.'
key_points: Apple introduced the Apple Watch Series 12, featuring a new 'Audio Intelligence' system starting at £369 and launching on 18 September.
The watch's controversial 'Live Rewind' and 'Siri Recap' tools allow users to review text snippets and summaries of recent conversations.
Apple also debuted its first foldable iPhone, dubbed the iPhone Duo, alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max.
New updates include AirPods 5 with improved Active Noise Cancellation and an enhanced Health app powered by Apple Intelligence.

title: Google has removed the Pixel Tablet from its store - Engadget
author: Mariella Moon
content:
Google has removed the Pixel Tablet from its store
The three-year-old tablet may have already been discontinued.
We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.
Google seems to have removed the Pixel Tablet from its store and has even taken out the "Tablet" option from its menu at the top of its homepage. The device's removal from the Google Store was first noticed by Jetstream, which also reported a few days ago that the device was already marked "Out of stock."
Now that Google has removed the product itself from its store, the device may have already been discontinued, as the publication notes. We asked Google for confirmation whether it truly has phased out the tablet and will update this post when we hear back. Google has yet to remove the listings for Pixel Tablet accessories. However, most of them, such as the the Pixel Tablet Case and Charging Speaker Dock, are no longer in stock. You can only "get notified" for when they become available again, if Google does restock them. At the moment, only the Wasserstein Pixel Tablet Speaker Stand is available for purchase.
Google announced the Pixel Tablet at I/O 2023. The company sold it for $899 at launch with a charging speaker base, and the twofer offering made that price point more attractive. It's no longer for sale on Amazon, as well, and its Best Buy listing says the "item is no longer available in new condition."
summary: Google has removed the Pixel Tablet from its official store and taken the "Tablet" option off its homepage menu, indicating the device may be discontinued. The three-year-old device and most of its official accessories are currently out of stock. The tablet is also unavailable for purchase as new on Amazon and Best Buy.
key_points: Google removed the Pixel Tablet from its online store and top menu.
The device may have been quietly discontinued after launching at I/O 2023.
Most official accessories, including the case and charging dock, are out of stock.
Retailers like Amazon and Best Buy no longer have the tablet available for purchase in new condition.

title: It’s the year of smartphone price hikes
author: Stevie Bonifield
content:
Paying more for a new phone seems almost unavoidable after Apple’s event today. The new iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max start at $1,199 and $1,299, respectively — a $100 price hike over their predecessors. You can’t dodge the price hike by opting for an older iPhone, either, because Apple raised prices on those by $100, too. And it’s not just Apple. This year, the $100 price hike has been a trend across the industry.
It’s the year of smartphone price hikes
Apple, Google, and Samsung’s new phones have two things in common: They include a foldable and they cost more.
![268735_iPhone_18_Pro_NPatel_0005](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/268735_iPhone_18_Pro_NPatel_0005.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0%2C0%2C100%2C100&w=2400)
![268735_iPhone_18_Pro_NPatel_0005](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/268735_iPhone_18_Pro_NPatel_0005.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0%2C0%2C100%2C100&w=2400)
Google and Samsung followed the same formula as Apple when they each launched new phones over the past few months. The Pixel 11 starts at $899, up from $799 for last year’s Pixel 10. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra launched at $2,099, $100 more than the Galaxy Z Fold 7 it replaced.
You could try looking for a phone from a brand outside the big three, but the price hikes persist there, too. Sony’s new Xperia 10 VIII costs £150 more, and this year’s Moto Razr phones also cost $100 more than their predecessors, each offering little to no significant upgrades to go with their higher prices. Smartphone sales data shows that the market for phones under $100 may be on its way to completely disappearing.
The price hikes stem from ongoing component shortages, driven by AI data center buildouts, that could last years and aren’t showing any signs of letting up. RAM price hikes have been among the most severe. Nothing CEO Carl Pei said earlier this year that memory costs for the Nothing Phone 4A had doubled by the time it launched. Nearly every component that goes into new phones, and other tech, is also getting pricier. Qualcomm, which makes the processors that power many new phones, raised prices on its chips earlier this month.
Apple was fashionably late to raise its phone prices, like it was late to launch a foldable, potentially signaling that both trends are here to stay.
summary: Smartphone prices are rising across the industry this year, driven by ongoing component shortages linked to AI data center buildouts. Major manufacturers like Apple, Google, and Samsung have all increased prices by $100 for their new devices, and brands outside the major three are following the same trend. These price hikes affect various models and older phones alike, with the sub-$100 phone market potentially disappearing.
key_points: Apple raised the starting prices of the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, as well as older iPhone models, by $100.
Google's Pixel 11 and Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra both launched with $100 price increases compared to their predecessors.
Other brands like Sony and Motorola also implemented price hikes ranging from $100 to £150 on their new devices.
Price increases are driven by severe component and memory shortages caused by AI data center buildouts, alongside higher chip prices from Qualcomm.

title: Everything Apple announced at the foldable iPhone Duo launch - Engadget
author: Kris Holt
content:
Everything Apple announced at the foldable iPhone Duo launch
The company also revealed the iPhone 18 Pro lineup, along with new Apple Watches and AirPods.
Apple executives — including newly minted CEO John Ternus — took center stage on Wednesday to unveil the company's latest iPhones and Apple Watches. The star of the show was the iPhone Duo, Apple's first foldable smartphone. The company also debuted the iPhone 18 Pro lineup. The base iPhone 18 may not arrive until the spring, when Apple is expected to reveal the iPhone Air 2 and iPhone 18e, in a shakeup of the usual iPhone release strategy.
In addition, Apple unveiled its latest wearables, the Apple Watch Series 13 and the Apple Watch Ultra 4. The company updated its AirPods as well.
Heading into the event, we knew that these iPhones and Apple Watches would debut alongside Siri AI, the revamped, Gemini-powered voice assistant that's at the heart of iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27, watchOS 27 and so on. Some earlier iPhones and Apple Watches — i.e. those compatible with Apple Intelligence — will support Siri AI as well, but Apple designed these latest devices in concert with the assistant. The public version of iOS 27 will bring Siri AI to compatible iPhones on September 14.
Siri AI will be available in English only at first. Support for French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish is coming in October. Note that Siri AI is delayed indefinitely in the EU. As with Apple Intelligence, it will not be available in China.
Meanwhile, Apple has increased the prices of older iPhones by $100. We'd usually see those drop when new models were announced. You can thank memory and storage supply issues for that.
Let's dive into everything Apple announced at its "Surprise and Shine" iPhone event.
iPhone Duo
The main attraction of this event was the long-rumored foldable iPhone. It was hardly a secret that Apple was working on such a device, especially after third-party companies started selling cases for the phone earlier this week.
The foldable is called the iPhone Duo. It was previously expected that Apple would call it the iPhone Ultra. Duo isn't exactly the most exciting name, but at least it's a logical one.
The book-style format Apple has opted for allows for a wide main display that's akin to a tablet. Essentially, it's a way for you to have iPad mini-style utility right in your pocket. Both displays even have Apple Pencil support.
The main display features a 7.6-inch Super Retina screen, which is quite a bit smaller than the 8.3-inch one on the iPad mini. Still, it's the biggest-ever display on an iPhone. There's a 5.4-inch screen on the exterior. (I would love an iPhone with a screen that size without the foldable aspect. I still miss the iPhone 5.)
When it's open, the iPhone Duo is the thinnest iPhone to date at 0.21 inches (5.2 mm). Folded up, it's 0.44 inches (11.3mm) thick. It weighs 8.96 ounces (254 grams).
The main screen has something new for an iPhone, an under-display camera. As a notch hater, I'm very happy to hear that. The exterior display. on the other hand, has a hole punch cut out for the camera.
The speakers are positioned on the top and bottom of the device, which is available in two colors, star white and night sky. The iPhone Duo runs on the same A20 Pro chip as the iPhone 18 Pro models (more on that in a bit).
It's an eSIM-only device, which was a decision Apple made to make more space for the battery. The company says iPhone Duo offers 44 hours of video playback on the external screen. If you use both displays equally, you'll get around 24 hours of use before you have to charge, Apple claims. It adds that five minutes of wired charging is enough to give you five hours of video-watching time on the external screen.
Smartphones with foldable displays have been around for quite some time, but Apple tends not to enter a product category until it's confident that it can get things right. It's extremely unlikely that the company would have moved into foldables until it was sure it cracked the hinge durability puzzle. A report earlier this year suggested Apple ran into an engineering hitch that might have caused a delay, but that turned out not to be the case.
As it turns out, the iPhone Duo is IP68 rated for water and dust protection. Apple notes that the hinge has carbon fiber support plates and there's a titanium frame and hinge cover. There's a nano texture on the display that features a scratch-resistant coating too.
The iPhone Duo does not have a dedicated telephoto camera. There's a 48MP main camera and an 48MP ultrawide. The device has some nifty camera tricks. For instance, you might not need a tripod, as you can prop the iPhone Duo up by itself. There's also a way for you to let the subject see the framing of a shot while you're lining it up, and a cool FaceTime feature allows people on both sides of the device to join the conversation.
It does not seem like there's a dedicated camera control button. Nor is there an Action Button, which is a bummer. That thing's super useful for quickly Shazamming a song!
One other common iPhone feature you won't find in the first iPhone Duo is Face ID. Perhaps this is to get around the need to have a TrueDepth camera system for each screen, even though each has a FaceTime camera. Much like on iPads, Apple built the Touch ID sensor into the side button (aka the wake/sleep button). You can unlock the device using an Apple Watch as well.
On the software side, you'll be able to multitask on the main screen. As with foldables from other companies, you can run two apps at once on the main display or even two instances of the same one.
Apple has shifted essential controls (such as the Home Screen dock and playback buttons for Apple Music) to the side of the external screen to free up vertical space. All of the company's own apps are optimized for the dual-display device. Some third-party partners are making use of the format too. For example, you can browse clips from Netflix on the smaller screen before hopping into the relevant show or movie on the main display.
StandBy mode works on both displays. You'll see that on the external screen when you prop the device up, even if you're not charging — despite rumors to the contrary, iPhone Duo does support MagSafe and Qi2 charging.
The iPhone Duo starts at $1,999 for a version with 256GB of storage. There are 512GB, 1TB and 2TB options. The latter will run you $3,199. Pre-orders open on October 16 and Apple's first foldable iPhone will be in customers' hands as soon as October 23.
An official case (in navy blue or sand) will run you $79. A folio case with a kickstand costs $129 and that's available in navy blue and taupe.
iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max
New Apple CEO John Ternus kicked off the presentation with a spiel about how the iPhone is "an intelligent personal hub," trying to position it at the center of your life (which it may well be already, let's be honest). He then transitioned into the first product announcements of the day, the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max.
Apple says the 18 Pro Max has the longest battery life of any iPhone to date with 45 hours of video playback. The iPhone 18 Pro is said to have the same battery life as the 17 Pro Max, so it should be good for around 36 hours of video playback. Those figures are for eSIM-only variants, which have a larger battery than those with a physical SIM slot (those will have two hours less video playback time).
The company says it'll take just 15 minutes to recharge to 50 percent of battery capacity over a wired connection, and just five minutes of charging time will seemingly get you seven hours of video-watching time on the 18 Pro Max. We'll have to test those claims ourselves, of course.
The iPhone 18 Pro models run on an A20 Pro chipset. The A20 Pro is a 2nm chip that has a six-core CPU with four efficiency cores and two "desktop class" super cores that are said to be 20 percent faster than the previous gen. It also has a seven-core GPU and a neural engine with 32 cores. Apple claims the A20 Pro delivers up to 40 percent improved graphics performance, which could come in handy for the iOS-exclusive Monster Hunter game the company showed off. Apple added that the chipset offers 50 percent more memory bandwidth than A19 Pro.
The latest phones have Apple's N1 chip to support Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread. They also have a new modem, the C2. Apple says this "delivers meaningfully faster uploads when compared to C1X while consuming 15 percent less energy." it supports mmWave in the US as well.
To help keep things cool while it's processing all of your Siri AI prompts and whatnot, the iPhone 18 Pro has a next-gen vapor chamber with three times the surface area of the one in the iPhone 17 Pro. Apple says it has 80 percent recycled stainless steel and graphite and offers a 40 percent performance improvement over the previous cooling system.
The iPhone 18 Pro has a new 48MP fusion main camera with a variable aperture. The camera system supports 4K and Dolby Vision HDR for timelapse recordings and you'll be able to apply cinematic effects after you capture footage. Pro controls will let you customize the camera experience too.
To help verify the authenticity of photos, Apple is introducing a feature called Apple Reference Image (which won't be available in the EU or China, unfortunately). This is built into a sensor in the iPhone 18 Pro's main camera. The company is also supporting the SynthID watermarking standard for images that are modified or generated using AI.
In addition, the Dynamic Island on the iPhone 18 Pro models is smaller than on previous devices. It can display three live activities simultaneously.
As expected, the iPhone 18 Pro devices are more expensive than their predecessors, due in large part to increases in memory and storage costs. Each costs $100 more than the respective iPhone 17 Pro device. The iPhone 18 Pro starts at $1,199 and the 18 Pro Max starts at $1,299. Pre-orders open this Saturday (September 12) and the phones will be available on September 18. There's a hot new burgundy color option to go with the black, silver and glacier variants.
Along with the US, eSIM-only versions of iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max will be available in Bahrain, Canada, Guam, Japan, Kuwait, Mexico, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the UAE and the US Virgin Islands.
We've had some hands-on time with the iPhone 18 Pro, so be sure to check out our initial impressions.
Apple Watch Series 12
Along with the new phones, Apple refreshed its smartwatches. The Apple Watch Series 12 has upgraded internals. Among other things, Apple says these improve the wearable's heart rate sensing capabilities. It can check your heart rate every five seconds, allowing Apple to offer a new complication with more detailed live data. The device will offer users a Readiness score too.
The claimed battery life is the same as the Apple Watch Series 11 at 24 hours, but charging is said to be faster. Apple says 15 minutes of charging will get you 12 hours of juice. The Apple Watch Series 12 runs on an S11 chip.
The biggest new capability Apple is touting this time around is called Audio Intelligence. This can pick up sounds in the environment and alert you to noises like alarms and a crying infant, potentially making it very valuable for folks with hearing impairments. The feature can also transcribe the last 15 seconds of a conversation. Siri can summarize your chat too. In addition, Shazam can constantly run in the background to help you identify whatever song is playing nearby.
Apple says it won't store recordings and the audio remains private. All of the Audio Intelligence features are optional.
The Apple Watch Series 12 starts at $399. It's available in 42mm and 46mm case sizes in a variety of designs, including a returning ceramic option. Pre-orders open today and the wearable will be available on September 18.
Apple Watch Ultra 4
As for the Apple Watch Ultra 4, you can expect battery life improvements. Apple says it runs for up to 50 hours in everyday use and 84 hours in low power mode. A 15-minute charge adds as much as 18 hours of battery life, according to Apple.
The Apple Watch Ultra 4 runs on the same S11 chip as the Apple Watch Series 12. It supports Audio Intelligence as well.
Both watch lineups include a fancy Hermès variant. Along with a watch face that offers an "illustration of the ocean's depths," the Apple Watch Hermès Ultra 4 includes a "Grand H titanium band featuring a built-in extension mechanism to conveniently adjust the band to fit over a wet suit."
The Apple Watch Ultra 4 starts at $799. Pre-orders open in more than 50 regions and countries today, and the latest model can be on your wrist as soon as September 18.
AirPods 5
The AirPods 5 come in two flavors. A $129 entry-level model features open-ear active noise cancellation (ANC), with Apple claiming it "removes up to 50 percent more external noise compared to AirPods 4." The company says there's a "more natural Transparency mode," as well as improved IP57 dust, sweat and water resistance compared with the previous gen.
You'll get up to four hours of listening time with ANC enabled, Apple says. With the charging case, you'll seemingly get up to 20 hours of battery life.
A $149 option includes all of that as well as a wireless charging case (which you can top up with an Apple Watch charger) and on-stem volume control. Apple says this version will run for up to five hours with ANC enabled. The charging case extends the total listening time to 22 hours, the company claims.
You can pre-order both AirPods 5 options today. They'll hit stores on September 18.
What Apple didn't announce
There are several products Apple is said to be working on that didn't make an appearance at the "Surprise and Shine" event. The company doesn't tend to reveal new iPads at its iPhone events, as it usually saves those until later in the fall. Reports suggest an iPad mini with an OLED display is in the works and we may still see that within the coming weeks. After the recent Mac mini and Mac Studio refreshes, you'll need to wait a bit longer for new Macs as well.
We've seen some leaks around the next AirPods Pro, which could have cameras. Rather than surreptitiously capturing video, these are said to take still images that Apple feeds into Visual Intelligence. That could make for some very useful accessibility features. A user with vision impairment wouldn't necessarily have to rely on much-maligned smart glasses with built-in cameras or point their smartphone's camera at something they need more information about.
Apple's long-expected smart home hub display was nowhere to be seen either. In truth, it makes sense for the company to keep the focus on iPhone and Apple Watch and reveal other products later. I wouldn't be surprised to see Apple running a smart home-focused event in the coming months to show off the smart display along with revamped Apple TV and HomePod models.
summary: Apple unveiled its first foldable smartphone, the iPhone Duo, alongside the iPhone 18 Pro lineup, new Apple Watches, and updated AirPods during its latest event led by CEO John Ternus. The event also highlighted Siri AI, a Gemini-powered voice assistant integrated across Apple's latest devices and operating systems. The new products feature advanced hardware upgrades, including the 2nm A20 Pro chip in the Pro models and innovative design elements such as an under-display camera on the foldable Duo.
key_points: Apple introduced the iPhone Duo, its first book-style foldable smartphone featuring a 7.6-inch main display and a 5.4-inch exterior screen.
The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max models are powered by the new 2nm A20 Pro chip and feature improved cooling systems, smaller Dynamic Islands, and upgraded 48MP main cameras.
Siri AI, a Gemini-powered assistant running on iOS 27 and other new operating systems, launches in English on September 14 with broader language support arriving in October.
Apple also announced new wearables, including the Apple Watch Series 12 with Audio Intelligence features and the Apple Watch Ultra 4.
Prices for the new iPhone models and older generations have increased by $100 due to memory and storage supply issues.

title: Apple Debuts iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max
author: Press Release by Nomad
content:
Wednesday, September 9th 2026
	
									
![Apple](https://tpucdn.com/images/news/apple-v1788270976.png) 
Apple today announced iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, delivering the most advanced pro camera system in an iPhone, and huge leaps in battery life and performance. The new 48MP Fusion Main camera, now with variable aperture, brings creative control that wasn't possible before, and new Pro controls let users customize their experience in the Camera app. Both models feature a smaller and even more useful Dynamic Island, as well as A20 Pro and a next-generation vapor chamber that together deliver the highest sustained performance in iPhone history. iPhone 18 Pro Max also delivers the largest increase in battery life ever on iPhone, thanks to advancements in Apple silicon and a larger battery. Featuring iOS 27 with Apple Intelligence and Siri AI, iPhone 18 Pro models bring powerful AI capabilities together with personal context to become an intelligent personal hub with privacy and security at its core.
iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max are available in four elegant finishes: black, silver, glacier, and an all-new burgundy. Pre-orders begin Saturday, September 12, with availability beginning Friday, September 18.
![](https://tpucdn.com/img/2ohe1KoEruYQpX5K_thm.jpg) 
![](https://tpucdn.com/img/BLO7jmfU2xJJIEfY_thm.jpg) 
![](https://tpucdn.com/img/GHNBYfThnh0e0KDW_thm.jpg) 
Greg Joswiak, Apple's senior vice president of Worldwide Marketing"With iPhone 18 Pro, we've made advancements to the areas our users care about most: camera, performance, battery, and intelligence. And we didn't just make incremental improvements in these areas—we took huge leaps forward to create the best Pro iPhone we've ever made. iPhone 18 Pro makes it easy for anyone to capture stunning photos and videos using variable aperture, while providing more versatility for creators and more control for pros. Paired with impactful upgrades to Photographic Styles and powerful video capabilities, iPhone 18 Pro unlocks entirely new ways for users to express themselves."
An Advanced Camera System That Unlocks More Creativity Across Photo and Video
The new 48MP Fusion Main camera with variable aperture is the most advanced camera Apple has ever made, bringing aperture control to iPhone for the first time along with even more creative control. Six laser-cut blades smoothly transition between different apertures, making it incredibly easy to capture the best shot by automatically adjusting for depth of field and lighting. Combined with a new sensor that improves image quality, the result is better low-light photography, crisper detail in the back of group photos, and more unique shots. Variable aperture also provides more control for creative pros by giving them the ability to manually adjust any of the four aperture settings in the Camera app, and an API is available to developers for even more control across the aperture range in their apps.
With a new computational imaging pipeline, the Main camera produces sharper, more detailed shots, and upgraded Photographic Styles with new texture and grain controls let users further dial in their desired appearance and have more creative control over their photos. Industry-leading video capabilities also become more versatile, with the ability to apply Cinematic effects after capture to videos shot at up to 60 FPS. In Time-lapse mode, users can now record videos in 4K and Dolby Vision HDR. Audio Mix also has new algorithms that deliver higher-quality voices and can now isolate music.
![](https://tpucdn.com/img/g9xKurhixw1siYOR_thm.jpg) 
![](https://tpucdn.com/img/A8uR5Nj8yFM0o8hz_thm.jpg) 
![](https://tpucdn.com/img/mTQXH5sfaDRkgzmU_thm.jpg) 
![](https://tpucdn.com/img/bw8NH2vA1TYEdHmF_thm.jpg) Pro controls is a new customizable experience in the Camera app for iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max that makes it easier than ever for users to access their most used settings and introduces new options for manual control. Users can now adjust settings such as lens aperture, shutter speed, and white balance, or use a histogram to check exposure levels throughout a scene.
Introducing Apple Reference Image
Users can now prove the authenticity of a photo taken on iPhone 18 Pro models with Apple Reference Image, powered by the new sensor in the Main camera that can sign every pixel it sees. When a photo is taken in the new Reference mode, the camera captures signed sensor data that Private Cloud Compute develops into an unalterable reference image. Reference images can be viewed in the Photos app alongside the main image, like a digital negative, to visually compare the two assets and determine if any edits were made. APIs are available in iOS, iPadOS, and macOS 27 for third-party apps to enable viewing of these reference images.
![](https://tpucdn.com/img/Sjt8sLRgv0dmWZ0Y_thm.jpg) Image metadata and upcoming support for the SynthID standard can also help users identify images generated or edited with AI. Together with Apple Reference Image, this set of features represents a multifaceted approach to image authenticity—vital for photojournalists, photographers, and everyday viewers.
An Even More Useful Dynamic Island
Using advanced display technology, the Dynamic Island is redesigned to create room for additional information. The upgraded Dynamic Island can now show three Live Activities at once, while continuing to enable Face ID for securely unlocking iPhone 18 Pro models, authenticating purchases, signing in to apps, and more.
A20 Pro: A Powerhouse for Pro Performance and AI
Built using the latest 2-nanometer process technology, A20 Pro sets a new bar for mobile computing. Featuring 50 percent more memory bandwidth than A19 Pro, the new 6-core CPU features integrated Neural Accelerators and is faster than the competition, while the new 7-core GPU design is up to 40 percent faster than A19 Pro—a significant upgrade for graphics rendering. A20 Pro also features a new Dual 16-core Neural Engine, which accelerates on-device AI models and computational photography, and includes 32 total cores for double the AI processing power of A19 Pro. With huge upgrades across the entire chip, A20 Pro is a powerhouse for everything from more advanced on-device AI workloads to demanding games, and is designed to deliver exceptional performance for years to come.
Both models feature N1, an Apple-designed wireless networking chip that enables Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread. iPhone 18 Pro introduces C2, Apple's next-generation cellular modem system, which brings AI-powered improvements to cellular quality and reliability. C2 delivers meaningfully faster uploads when compared to C1X while consuming 15 percent less energy, and now supports mmWave in the U.S.
A New Thermal Management System for Maximum Performance
A20 Pro introduces custom packaging inspired by M-series Apple silicon that places the silicon die side by side with the memory, removing the memory from the thermal path of the chip and allowing A20 Pro to attach directly to a next-generation vapor chamber. With new materials and three times more surface area than the previous generation on iPhone 17 Pro, the redesigned vapor chamber dramatically improves sustained performance and enables up to a 40 percent gain over the previous generation—the highest sustained performance yet.
Incredible Battery Life
iPhone 18 Pro models deliver a massive leap in battery life with new battery designs that leverage powerful silicon efficiencies. eSIM-only models deliver up to 36 hours of video playback on iPhone 18 Pro and up to 45 hours of video playback on iPhone 18 Pro Max. iPhone 18 Pro can also charge up to 50 percent in around 15 minutes, or wirelessly charge up to 50 percent in 30 minutes. On iPhone 18 Pro Max, five minutes of wired charging provides around seven hours of video playback, and based on a new battery usage model that leverages real-world data, it provides up to 30 hours of usage on a full charge.
Featuring iOS 27 with the Next Generation of Apple Intelligence and an All-New Siri
iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max give users access to Siri AI, rolling out in beta with iOS 27. Siri AI is an entirely new version of Siri powered by Apple Intelligence that is profoundly more personal, capable, and conversational. Both models bring powerful AI capabilities together with personal context to become an intelligent personal hub with privacy and security at its core.
Siri AI can draw on personal context understanding to help users find what they need in the moment across messages, emails, photos, and more; use onscreen awareness to take action related to the content on a user's screen; and answer questions about virtually any topic. Siri mode in the Camera app allows users to get information and take action on what's in front of them, and users can write with Siri by simply describing what they need. Additionally, Apple Intelligence makes apps smarter and more useful. Users can improve the composition of a photo after it's been taken with Spatial Reframing, Extend, and upgraded Clean Up. And now Image Playground offers photorealistic imagery. In Safari, Notify Me helps users monitor web pages for changes, like product restocks or price drops, and stay on top of updates. To protect users' privacy, Apple Intelligence uses on-device processing and Private Cloud Compute, which extends the privacy and security of iPhone into the cloud.
iOS 27 delivers an expansive set of improvements that make iPhone more responsive, reliable, and easy to use, along with refinements to the software design and more ways to personalize the appearance of Liquid Glass. Additionally, powerful and simple tools, based on expert guidance, give parents more flexible ways to manage what their kids can see, who they can talk to, and when they have access. iOS 27 also introduces iPhone Handoff, which allows users with supported carriers to easily switch back and forth between two iPhone models with the same phone number.
eSIM: A Flexible, Convenient, and Secure Connection
eSIM offers greater flexibility, better security, seamless connectivity compared to traditional physical SIM cards, and more battery life on eSIM-only models. An industry standard, eSIM is supported by over 500 carriers worldwide, including AT&T, T-Mobile, Verizon, and more. eSIM-only models of iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max will be available in Bahrain, Canada, Guam, Japan, Kuwait, Mexico, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, the U.S., and the U.S. Virgin Islands. These models feature an even larger battery, taking advantage of the space formerly occupied by the physical SIM to provide two additional hours of video playback.
Beautiful New Accessories
iPhone 18 Pro models introduce a range of new Silicone Cases, TechWoven Cases, Crossbody Straps, and FineWoven Wallets—all designed to complement the four beautiful finishes. The Clear Case features an updated design and is now compatible with the Crossbody Strap and Wrist Strap. The new Wrist Strap introduces a convenient, hands-free way to carry iPhone, AirPods Pro 2, or AirPods Pro 3. Woven with 100 percent recycled polyester yarns and embedded with flexible magnets that keep it neatly fitted together, the Wrist Strap will be available in six colors: black, taupe, olive, crisp blue, magenta, and burgundy.
![](https://tpucdn.com/img/wFCq2GVEWoAM4K72_thm.jpg) 
![](https://tpucdn.com/img/wCz6StkYZ5lyxn2w_thm.jpg) 
![](https://tpucdn.com/img/9yFFCnGYdwTMalFF_thm.jpg) iPhone 18 Pro and the Environment
iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max were built with the environment in mind, and drive progress toward Apple's ambitious plan to be carbon-neutral across its entire footprint by 2030. Both models are made with 40 percent recycled content overall, including 100 percent recycled cobalt in the battery and 85 percent recycled aluminium in the enclosure. They are manufactured with 50 percent renewable energy, like wind and solar, across the supply chain, and meet Apple's high standards for energy efficiency and safe chemistry. Like all Apple products, their paper packaging is 100 percent fiber-based and can be easily recycled at home.
Pricing and Availability
iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max will be available in 256 GB, 512 GB, 1 TB, and 2 TB storage capacities. Available in burgundy, glacier, silver, and black, iPhone 18 Pro starts at $1,199 (U.S.) or $49.95 (U.S.) per month, and iPhone 18 Pro Max starts at $1,299 (U.S.) or $54.12 (U.S.) per month for 24 months.
Apple offers great ways to save and upgrade to the latest iPhone models. With Apple Trade In, customers trading in iPhone 13 or later can get $175 to $885 (U.S.) in credit instantly. Apple also partners with select carriers to offer incredible deals, and customers can get up to $1,200 (U.S.) in credits when they trade in iPhone 14 or later—in any condition—to put toward iPhone 18 Pro or iPhone 18 Pro Max. Customers can take advantage of carrier deals by visiting the Apple Store online or an Apple Store location. For carrier deal eligibility requirements and more details, see apple.com/shop/buy-iphone/carrier-offers. To see what their device is worth and for trade-in terms and conditions, customers can visit apple.com/shop/trade-in.
Apple Upgrade, a leasing program provided by Klarna and available in the U.S., gives eligible customers monthly payment options for iPhone 18 Pro, with 12- and 24-month leasing terms starting as low as $34.99 (U.S.) per month for 24 months. For more information, visit apple.com/shop/apple-upgrade.
Customers in more than 65 countries and regions, including Australia, Brazil, Canada, China, Colombia, France, Germany, India, Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, Singapore, South Korea, Türkiye, the UAE, the UK, the U.S., and Vietnam, will be able to pre-order iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max beginning at 5 a.m. PT this Saturday, September 12, with availability beginning Friday, September 18. iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max will be available in 20 other countries and regions beginning Friday, September 25.
A TechWoven Case with MagSafe will be available for $59 (U.S.) in black, chambray blue, taupe, olive, mulberry, and burgundy. A Clear Case with MagSafe will be available for $49 (U.S.), and a Silicone Case with MagSafe will be available for $49 (U.S.) in black, navy blue, crisp blue, olive, burgundy, and magenta. A FineWoven Wallet with MagSafe will be available for $59 (U.S.) in black, navy blue, wildflower blue, olive, magenta, and burgundy.
A Wrist Strap will be available for $29 (U.S.). A Crossbody Strap will be available for $59 (U.S.) in black, navy blue, taupe, sand, olive, crisp blue, magenta, burgundy, and light gray.
iOS 27 will be available as a free software update on Monday, September 14. Some features may not be available in all languages or regions, and availability may vary due to local laws and regulations. For more information about availability, visit apple.com.
Apple Intelligence will be available with iOS 27 on Monday, September 14, for users with an Apple Intelligence-enabled device set to a supported language. Apple Intelligence is available with support for these languages: English, Danish, Dutch, French, German, Italian, Norwegian, Portuguese, Spanish, Swedish, Turkish, Vietnamese, Chinese (simplified), Chinese (traditional), Japanese, and Korean. Some features may not be available in all regions or languages. For feature and language availability and system requirements, see apple.com/apple-intelligence.
Siri AI is rolling out with iOS 27 as a beta on Monday, September 14, for users with a supported device set to English, with support for French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish coming in October. Some features may not be available in all regions or languages.
When outside of cellular and Wi-Fi coverage, Apple's groundbreaking satellite features help iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max users stay connected and get assistance when it matters most. Apple is extending free access to satellite features for an additional year for existing iPhone 14, iPhone 15, and iPhone 16 users. The free trial will be extended for iPhone 14, iPhone 15, and iPhone 16 users who have activated their device in a country that supports Apple's satellite features prior to midnight PT on September 9. For satellite feature availability, visit support.apple.com/en-us/105097.
AppleCare delivers exceptional service and support, with flexible options for Apple users. Customers can choose AppleCare+ to cover their new iPhone, or, in available markets, AppleCare One to protect multiple products in one simple plan. Both plans include coverage for accidents like drops and spills, theft and loss protection on eligible products, battery replacement service, and priority support from Apple Experts. In the U.S., customers can also choose AppleCare One Family, which extends that same coverage to every eligible device across an Apple Family Sharing group for one fixed monthly price. For more information, visit apple.com/applecare.
iCloud+ plans start at just $0.99 (U.S.) per month, providing additional storage to keep photos, videos, files, and more safe in the cloud and accessible across devices. iCloud+ also gives access to premium features such as event creation in the Apple Invites app, as well as Private Relay, Hide My Email, custom email domains, and HomeKit Secure Video. With Family Sharing, users can share their subscription with five other family members at no extra cost. For more information and feature availability, visit apple.com/icloud and apple.com/ios/feature-availability.
New and qualified returning subscribers who purchase iPhone 18 Pro or iPhone 18 Pro Max can unlock three months of Apple One for free. Apple One bundles up to six Apple services—including Apple TV, Apple Music, up to 2 TB of iCloud+ storage, and more—into one convenient plan across multiple Apple devices. This offer is available in select countries and regions with an eligible new iPhone, iPad, or Mac beginning September 17. Service availability varies by region. Learn more about Apple One at apple.com/apple-one.
